Vide this award, I shall dispose of the present claim petition filed under Section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, on behalf of the petitioner Rakesh Kumar seeking compensation on account of injuries suffered by him in a motor vehicular accident.

2. Briefly stated the facts as narrated by the petitioner are that on 13.04.2012, he was travelling as pillion rider on motorcycle bearing no. UP16L-2674 (in short "offending vehicle"), being driven by Naresh Babu @ Gopal (respondent no.1) at high speed and when they reached near Sector-33, Noida Chowk, within the jurisdiction of PS Sector-34, Noida, U.P., one stray animal (neel cow) suddenly came on the road, due to which driver lost control over the motorcycle and hit it against the divider on road.
As a result, both the occupants of motorcycle fell down on road and sustained grievous injuries.
They both were taken to Prakash Hospital, where their MLCs were prepared.

sentences.text: It has been alleged that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
With these submissions, petitioner has claimed a compensation of Rs.20 lakhs along with interest @ 12% from the date of filing of the petition till its realization from the respondents.
3. On notice of the claim petition, only respondent no.2 and 3 appeared and filed their written-statements.

Respondent no.1 could not be served by way of ordinary process and then he was got served by way of publication in newspaper Rashtriya Sahara, dated 22.08.2017 but still he did not put appearance and was proceeded ex-parte.

4. In written-statement filed by respondent no.2, it has been contended that the petition is not maintainable against the answering respondent as it is based upon false, frivolous and concocted facts and deserves to be rejected outrightly.
It is stated that as driver/ respondent no.1 was the employee of answering respondent and he expired at the time of accident.

It is contended that petitioner has nowhere stated in the petition as in what capacity he was travelling on the vehicle in question as the petitioner is unknown to the deceased driver as well as to the answering respondent who had not authorized his employee/ driver to allow anyone to use or travel the vehicle and therefore, any unauthorized act on the part of employee/ driver i.e. allegedly giving lift to anyone is illegal and cannot make the answering respondent liable.
5.

It is further contended that even if the version of petitioner that due to sudden coming of animal in front of vehicle, driver could not control the vehicle and hit it against the divider, is deemed correct then it is clear that the accident took place due to animal's suddenly coming in front of vehicle and not due to any alleged negligence on the part of driver/ respondent no.1.
It is also contended that there is no justification for allegedly giving GD entry on 29.10.2012 by the petitioner after almost 6-7 months of the date of accident.
With these submissions, the prayer for dismissal of the claim petition has been made.

6. Respondent no.3/insurance company in its written statement admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with it but contended that no liability can be fastened upon it unless it is proved that respondent no.1 was having valid and effective driving license on the date of accident.

It is stated that petition is not maintainable as petitioner is not a third party and further no separate premium was paid for the pillion rider by the insured.
7.

Upon completion of pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor, vide order dated 17.10.2017,
framed the following issues:
i).

Whether respondent no.1 was driving motorcycle bearing no. UP16L-2674 on 13.04.2012, near Sector-33, Noida Chowk, U.P. at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit against Rakesh Kumar and sustained injuries?

OPP.
ii).
Whether the petitioner is entitled for any compensation, if so, to what amount?

sentences.text: The evidence was closed and thereafter, I heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsel for the opposite parties.
I have also perused the evidence and entire material placed on record.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1
Whether

respondent no.1 was driving motorcycle bearing no.
UP16L-2674 on 13.04.2012, near Sector-33, Noida Chowk, U.P. at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit against Rakesh Kumar and sustained injuries?
OPP 11.

On this issue, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and deposed that on 13.04.2012, he was travelling from office to home after finishing duty, as pillion rider on motorcycle no. UP16L-2674,
which was driven by one Naresh Babu @ Gopal at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner.

He requested the driver Naresh Babu @ Gopal to drive the motorcycle at a normal speed but driver did not pay any heed on his request and when they reached near Sector-33, Noida Chowk, the driver could not control over the motorcycle and hit it against the divider, due to which they both fell down on road and sustained grievous injuries and were taken to Prakash Hospital, Noida and later on driver died.
PW1 further stated that motorcycle driver was negligent in driving the motorcycle and the accident and was solely responsible for causing the accident.

12. PW1 further deposed that after the accident, he was removed to Prakash Hospital, where his MLC was prepared and his injuries were managed but since relatives were not satisfied, he was got discharged from the hospital on 19.04.2012.

Petitioner (PW1) stated that thereafter, he was got admitted in Holy Family Hospital, where he remained hospitalized from 19.04.2012 to 26.04.2012 and during this period his all five toes (right) were amputated and he again remained admitted in said hospital from 07.05.2012 to 12.05.2012.

In support of his deposition, petitioner relied upon the discharge summaries Ex.PW1/2, Ex.PW1/3 and Ex.PW1/4, medical treatment record Ex.PW1/5 and medical bills Ex.PW1/6 to Ex.PW1/9, disability certificate Ex.PW1/10 and copy of GD entry Ex.PW1/11.
12.

Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that the testimony of petitioner (PW1), which is duly supported by the documentary evidence as relied upon by the petitioner, is sufficient to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that respondent no.1 caused the accident of petitioner by driving the offending vehicle in rash and negligent manner.

14. On the other hand, learned counsel for the insurance company argued that the present claim case is not maintainable at all because the police complaint in the form of GD no.22, given by the petitioner nowhere mentioned about the negligence on the part of deceased driver.

15. Further, learned counsel for respondent no.2 has also argued that petitioner has failed to prove on record that he was travelling as a pillion rider on the motorcycle being driven by respondent no.1 and that the petitioner suffered injuries while sitting as pillion rider on the motorcycle, being driven by respondent no.1 in rash and negligent manner.
Further, learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also pointed out various contradictions in the testimony of petitioner (PW1).

sentences.text: I have perused the evidence and documents placed on record in the light of arguments addressed by learned counsel for the parties and found several contradictions in the testimony of petitioner (PW1).

It is noted that that petitioner (PW1) in his testimony stateds that he had not informed the doctors in hospital about the accident when he got conscious but he voluntarily added that due to pain he was not in a position to speak and he stated that he had informed the police officials about the accident when PCR officials took him to the hospital.

In support of his said deposition, copy of Police Information Book, dated 13.04.2012, maintained by Prakash Hospital Pvt. Ltd., is found placed on record, which reflects the date and time of accident as 02:00 a.m. on 13.04.2012.

17. Perusal of this document reveals that injured Rakesh (petitioner) along with Naresh Babu (respondent no.1) was brought to the hospital immediately after the accident i.e. at 02:10 a.m. on 13.04.2012, and it is also mentioned that injured was going on two wheeler which was hit by an unknown vehicle at Red Light of NTPC, Sector-33, Noida.

Thus, from the deposition of petitioner in the light of copy of Police Information Book, dated 13.04.2012, at the most it can only be established on record that petitioner met with an accident and he along with respondent no.1 were brought to the hospital in injured condition but it nowhere indicates that respondent no.1 was driving the motorcycle and caused the accident while driving it in in rash and negligence manner.
18.

Further, in his testimony before this Tribunal, petitioner (PW1) stated that he went to police when he was able to walk to inquire about his complaint but he was informed that the driver had died in the accident and he further stated that he does not know if the police filed any closure report on his complaint before criminal court but surprisingly, he was unable to show any complaint given to police about the negligent driving of motorcycle by its driver.
19.
Further, it is noted that the carbon copy of letter dated 29.10.2012, having signature and seal of PS Sector-24, Noida has been placed on record.
The said information was taken on police record in the form of GD no. 22, dated 29.10.2012, which has been relied upon by petitioner as Ex.PW1/11.

Perusal of said document shows that it was a letter by petitioner Rakesh Kumar addressed to SHO,
PS Sector-24, Noida informing about occurrence of accident, seeking legal action.

In the said letter,
petitioner informed that he along with his friend Gopal (respondent no.1) was going home from office at 01:00 night on 13.04.2012 on motorcycle no. UP16HL-2674, being driven by Gopal and when they reached near Sector-33 Crossing, all of a sudden an animal came on road and in order to save that animal, motorcycle struck against the divider on road and again mentioned that in order to save an unknown vehicle.
Also, the petitioner mentioned that as a result, they both got injured.
The petitioner further mentioned that PCR took them to Prakash Hospital, where Gopal died and he sustained injury.
He stated he could not report the accident in time as he was undergoing treatment.

20. Thus, it is clear from above evidence and documents that it was about 6 months after the accident on 29.10.2012 only when for the first time, petitioner informed the police about the accident vide GD no.22 and in that information, he did not mention even a single word about the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by respondent no.1.
21.

Further, the treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner show that after the accident, petitioner remained hospitalized in Prakash Hospital, Noida from 13.04.2012 to Rakesh Kumar vs Kanwar Bahadur on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190151175/
5 19.04.2012 and thereafter, he remained admitted in Holy Family Hospital, Delhi from 19.04.2012 to 26.04.2012 and then from 07.05.2012 to 12.05.2012.
Except these documents, no other document to show any further treatment of petitioner has been placed on record.

22. It is also noteworthy that during cross-examination of petitioner (PW1), suggestion was also put to him that he was hit by some unknown vehicle and in order to claim the compensation he falsely shown the involvement of alleged offending vehicle after eight months in the month of October 2012.
Though, petitioner denied the said suggestion but admitted that he has no medical certificate to show that he was advised bed rest for eight months.

In view of the period of treatment reflected from the aforementioned treatment record as per which petitioner remained hospitalized for the third occasion from 07.05.2012 to 12.05.2012, I do not find any force in the reason of delay in reporting the accident to police on 29.10.2022 as per GD no. 22.

Thus, it is quite clear from the above that the allegations against the deceased driver/ respondent no.1 that he was driving the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner appears to be an afterthought only.

23. In view of above discussion, I may observe that the even the minimum requirements as expected from the petitioner to prove his case on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, have not been taken care of in this case.

In the instant case, no documentary evidence in the form of FIR, Site Plan,
Seizure Memo and Mechanical Inspection Report of offending vehicle or any police proceedings regarding investigation of the accident have been brought on record by the petitioner in support of his version to the rash and negligent driving by respondent no.1.

Only carbon copy of GD no. 22,
dated 29.10.2012, which has been relied upon by petitioner as Ex.PW1/11, has been placed on record, which too has not been proved by the petitioner as per law.

Otherwise also, on perusal of said DD recorded about 6 after month of the accident, shows only the information of accident given by petitioner and it nowhere mentions even a single word alleging the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
24.

For the aforesaid reasons, it is held that evidence led by the petitioner is neither convincing nor sufficient to prove that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent No.1.
Therefore, issue No.1 is decided against the petitioner.
Now, no further finding is required to be given in respect of other issues as the decision of the issue no.1 against petitioner is sufficient to decide the claim petition.
25. The present claim petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
No order as to costs.
File be consigned to Record Room.

Announced in open court (Shailender Malik)
on 18.09.2023 PO MACT-02, Shahdara,
 Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
